ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لَا نُضِيعُ أَجْرَ مَنْ أَحْسَنَ عَمَلًا (٣٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): concerning the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» there are three views. The first: it is «أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ», and what lies between them is a sound, well-placed parenthesis (muʿtariḍ). The second: its implied form is "We do not let the reward of whoever does good work among them go to waste", the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) having been omitted because it is known. The third: His saying (مَنْ أَحْسَنَ) is general, so «those who believed and did righteous deeds» fall within it, and this dispenses with a pronoun, just as the inclusion of Zayd under «the man» in the chapter of niʿma dispenses with a pronoun returning to it.
On these two [latter] views, the khabar of «إِنَّ» has been made the clause that contains «إِنَّ».

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ عَدْنٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهِمُ الْأَنْهَارُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَيَلْبَسُونَ ثِيَابًا خُضْرًا مِنْ سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ نِعْمَ الثَّوَابُ وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا (٣١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ): «مِنْ» may be redundant (zāʾida) according to the view of al-Akhfash; this is indicated by His saying (وَحُلُّوا أَسَاوِرَ).
It may also be non-redundant, i.e. "something of bracelets", in which case it serves to specify the genus or to denote part (tabʿīḍ).
And (مِنْ ذَهَبٍ): «مِنْ» in it specifies the genus or denotes part; its position is genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of «أَسَاوِرَ». It may also be attached to «يُحَلَّوْنَ».
«أَسَاوِرُ» is the plural of «أَسْوِرَة», and «أَسْوِرَة» is the plural of «سِوَار». It is also said: it is the plural of «أُسْوَار».
(مُتَّكِئِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the pronoun in «تَحْتِهِمْ», or from the pronoun in «يُحَلَّوْنَ», or in «يَلْبَسُونَ».
«السُّنْدُس» is the plural of «سُنْدُسَة», and «إِسْتَبْرَق» is the plural of «إِسْتَبْرَقَة»; it is also said that they are both generic nouns (jins).

ukberi-tibyan:32-34.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ جَعَلْنَا لِأَحَدِهِمَا جَنَّتَيْنِ مِنْ أَعْنَابٍ وَحَفَفْنَاهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمَا زَرْعًا (٣٢) كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا وَلَمْ تَظْلِمْ مِنْهُ شَيْئًا وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلَالَهُمَا نَهَرًا (٣٣) وَكَانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ فَقَالَ لِصَاحِبِهِ وَهُوَ يُحَاوِرُهُ أَنَا أَكْثَرُ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَأَعَزُّ نَفَرًا (٣٤))
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلًا رَجُلَيْنِ): the implied form is "a parable, the parable of two men".
And (جَعَلْنَا): it is an explanation of the parable, so it has no grammatical position. Its position may also be accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of «رَجُلَيْنِ», as when you say: "I passed by two men, for one of whom a garden was made". (كِلْتَا الْجَنَّتَيْنِ): mubtadaʾ (subject), and (آتَتْ) is its khabar (predicate); the pronoun is singular, construed according to the wording of «كِلْتَا». And (فَجَّرْنَا) is read with the light form and with the doubled form; and (خِلَالَهُمَا) is an adverb (ẓarf).
«الثُّمُر», with two ḍammas, is the plural of «ثِمَار», so it is a plural of a plural, like «كِتَاب» and «كُتُب». The mīm may also be made quiescent for lightness. And it is read (ثَمَرٌ), the plural of «ثَمَرَة».

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ وَهُوَ ظَالِمٌ لِنَفْسِهِ قَالَ مَا أَظُنُّ أَنْ تَبِيدَ هَذِهِ أَبَدًا (٣٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَدَخَلَ جَنَّتَهُ): He used the singular and did not say «جَنَّتَيْهِ» (his two gardens) only because both were his property, so they became like a single thing.
It is also said: [it is] by making do with the one instead of the two, just as one makes do with the singular instead of the plural; this is like the saying of al-Hudhalī:
وَالْعَيْنُ بَعْدَهُمُ كَأَنَّ حِدَاقَهَا ... سُمِلَتْ بِشَوْكٍ فَهِيَ عُورٌ تَدْمَعُ
("And the eye after them — it is as if its pupils were gouged with thorns, so they are blind, shedding tears": the singular «العين» is used for both eyes.)

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا أَظُنُّ السَّاعَةَ قَائِمَةً وَلَئِنْ رُدِدْتُ إِلَى رَبِّي لَأَجِدَنَّ خَيْرًا مِنْهَا مُنْقَلَبًا (٣٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خَيْرًا مِنْهَا): it is read in the singular, the pronoun referring to his garden; and in the dual [«مِنْهُمَا»], the pronoun referring to the two gardens.

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَكِنَّا هُوَ اللَّهُ رَبِّي وَلَا أُشْرِكُ بِرَبِّي أَحَدًا (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَكِنَّا): the original form is «لَكِنْ أَنَا»; the vowel of the hamza was transferred to the nūn — it is also said: [the hamza] was simply dropped — and the nūn was assimilated into the nūn. The best usage is to drop the alif in continuous recitation (waṣl) and to keep it when pausing (waqf), because «أَنَا» behaves that way, the alif in it being an addition to show the vowel.
It is also read with the alif kept in both cases. «أَنَا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), «هُوَ» is a second mubtadaʾ, «اللَّهُ» is a third mubtadaʾ, and «رَبِّي» is the khabar (predicate); the yāʾ refers back to the first mubtadaʾ.
It cannot be the doubled «لَكِنَّ» that governs the accusative, for if it were so, «هُوَ» would not occur after it, since it is a nominative pronoun. The name of Allah may also be a badal (substitute) from «هُوَ».

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَوْلَا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ إِنْ تَرَنِ أَنَا أَقَلَّ مِنْكَ مَالًا وَوَلَدًا (٣٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا شَاءَ اللَّهُ): concerning «مَا» there are two views. The first: it means «الَّذِي» (that which); it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is what Allah has willed". The second: it is conditional, in the position of the accusative by «يَشَاءُ», and the apodosis (jawāb) is omitted, i.e. "whatever Allah wills comes to be".
(إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ): in the position of the nominative as its khabar [i.e. the khabar of «لَا»].
(أَنَا): concerning it there are two views. The first: it is a separating pronoun (fāṣila) between the two objects. The second: it is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first object, so its position is accusative.
And it is read (أَقَلُّ) in the nominative, on the basis that «أَنَا» is a mubtadaʾ and «أَقَلُّ» its khabar, the clause being in the position of the second object.

ukberi-tibyan:41-41.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَعَسَى رَبِّي أَنْ يُؤْتِيَنِ خَيْرًا مِنْ جَنَّتِكَ وَيُرْسِلَ عَلَيْهَا حُسْبَانًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَتُصْبِحَ صَعِيدًا زَلَقًا أَوْ يُصْبِحَ مَاؤُهَا غَوْرًا فَلَنْ تَسْتَطِيعَ لَهُ طَلَبًا (٤١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حُسْبَانًا): it is the plural of «حُسْبَانَة».
And (غَوْرًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the sense of the active participle, i.e. «غَائِرًا» (sinking away).
It is also said: the implied form is «ذَا غَوْرٍ» (having sinking).

ukberi-tibyan:42-42.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأُحِيطَ بِثَمَرِهِ فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ عَلَى مَا أَنْفَقَ فِيهَا وَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا وَيَقُولُ يَا لَيْتَنِي لَمْ أُشْرِكْ بِرَبِّي أَحَدًا (٤٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ): this is the well-known [reading]. It is also read «تَقَلَّبُ», i.e. «تَتَقَلَّبُ كَفَّاهُ» (his palms turn over), with the nominative.
(عَلَى مَا أَنْفَقَ): it may be attached to «يُقَلِّبُ», or be a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "grieving over what he had spent on it", that is, on its cultivation.
And (يَقُولُ): it may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «يُقَلِّبُ», or conjoined to «يُقَلِّبُ».

ukberi-tibyan:43-43.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ فِئَةٌ يَنْصُرُونَهُ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مُنْتَصِرًا (٤٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَهُ): it is read with tāʾ and with yāʾ, and both are clear.
(يَنْصُرُونَهُ): construed according to the meaning, because the «فِئَة» (party) is people; had it been «تَنْصُرُهُ», it would have been according to the wording.

ukberi-tibyan:44-44.t:
Allah the Exalted says: {هُنَالك الْولَايَة لله الْحق هُوَ خير ثَوابًا وَخير عقبا}
His saying, Exalted is He: (هُنَالِكَ): concerning it there are two views. The first: it is an adverb (ẓarf), governed by the sense of stability (istiqrār) in «لِلَّهِ»; «الْوَلَايَةُ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لِلَّهِ» the khabar (predicate). The second: «هُنَالِكَ» is the khabar of «الْوَلَايَة», and «الْوَلَايَةُ» is made nominative by it; «لِلَّهِ» is then attached to the adverb, or to what governs the adverb, or to «الْوَلَايَة».
It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْوَلَايَة», in which case it is attached to an omitted [word].
And (الْوَلَايَةُ): with kasra and with fatḥa — two dialectal forms. It is also said: the kasra is for rulership and the fatḥa for support.
And (الْحَقُّ) in the nominative: an adjective of «الْوَلَايَة», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it (fem.) is the truth" or "He is the truth".
It may also be a mubtadaʾ, with «هُوَ خَيْرٌ» as its khabar.
It is also read in the genitive, as a naʿt (adjective) of «اللَّه», Exalted is He.

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ نَبَاتُ الْأَرْضِ فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيمًا تَذْرُوهُ الرِّيَاحُ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ مُقْتَدِرًا (٤٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَاضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَثَلَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا): you may take «اضْرِبْ» in the sense of «اذْكُرْ» (mention), so that it takes one object; on this view «كَمَاءٍ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is like water".
Or it may be in the sense of «صَيَّرَ» (make into), so that «كَمَاءٍ» is a second object.
(فَاخْتَلَطَ بِهِ): this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] Yūnus.
(تَذْرُوهُ): it is from «ذَرَتِ الرِّيحُ تَذْرُوهُ ذَرْوًا», i.e. it scattered [it].
One also says «ذَرَتْ تَذْرِي», and it has been read thus. And one says «أَذْرَتْ تُذْرِي», as when you say «أَذْرَيْتُهُ عَنْ فَرَسِهِ» when you have thrown him off his horse; and it has been read thus as well.

ukberi-tibyan:47-47.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا (٤٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الْجِبَالَ): i.e. "and mention the day".
It is also said: it is conjoined to «عِنْدِ رَبِّكَ», i.e. "righteous deeds are better with Allah, and better on the day We set the mountains in motion". In «نُسَيِّرُ» there are several readings, all of them clear.
(وَتَرَى): the address is to the Prophet ﷺ; it is also said: to every human being.
And (بَارِزَةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ): in the position of a ḥāl, with «قَدْ» intended, i.e. «وَقَدْ حَشَرْنَاهُمْ» (when We had already gathered them).

ukberi-tibyan:48-48.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَعُرِضُوا عَلَى رَبِّكَ صَفًّا لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ بَلْ زَعَمْتُمْ أَلَّنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِدًا (٤٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (صَفًّا): a ḥāl (circumstantial) meaning «مُصْطَفِّينَ» (lined up), i.e. «مَصْفُوفِينَ» (arranged in rows). The implied form is: "it is said to them: «لَقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا»", or [it is] "saying to them" [as] an object, so it is also a ḥāl. [Translator's note: the wording «أَوْ مَفْعُولًا لَهُمْ» appears garbled in the source; it is likely «أَوْ مَقُولًا لَهُمْ», "or: it having been said to them", which would make it a ḥāl as well.]
And (بَلْ): here it is for moving from one topic to another.

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَوُضِعَ الْكِتَابُ فَتَرَى الْمُجْرِمِينَ مُشْفِقِينَ مِمَّا فِيهِ وَيَقُولُونَ يَا وَيْلَتَنَا مَالِ هَذَا الْكِتَابِ لَا يُغَادِرُ صَغِيرَةً وَلَا كَبِيرَةً إِلَّا أَحْصَاهَا وَوَجَدُوا مَا عَمِلُوا حَاضِرًا وَلَا يَظْلِمُ رَبُّكَ أَحَدًا (٤٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يُغَادِرُ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْكِتَاب».

ukberi-tibyan:50-50.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ اسْجُدُوا لِآدَمَ فَسَجَدُوا إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ كَانَ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ أَفَتَتَّخِذُونَهُ وَذُرِّيَّتَهُ أَوْلِيَاءَ مِنْ دُونِي وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ بِئْسَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ بَدَلًا (٥٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قُلْنَا): i.e. "and mention".
(إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ): an exception (istithnāʾ) from outside the genus; it is also said: from the same genus.
And (كَانَ مِنَ الْجِنِّ): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «قَدْ» intended along with it.
(فَفَسَقَ): the fāʾ was brought in only because the meaning is "except Iblīs: he refused, and so he transgressed".
(بِئْسَ): its noun [i.e. its agent] is latent (muḍmar) in it, and the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, i.e. "how evil a substitute are he and his offspring".
And (لِلظَّالِمِينَ): a ḥāl from «بَدَلًا»; it is also said: it is attached to «بِئْسَ».

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ خَلْقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَلَا خَلْقَ أَنْفُسِهِمْ وَمَا كُنْتُ مُتَّخِذَ الْمُضِلِّينَ عَضُدًا (٥١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا أَشْهَدْتُهُمْ): i.e. Iblīs and his offspring. It is also read (أَشْهَدْنَاهُمْ).
(عَضُدًا): it is read with fatḥa on the ʿayn and ḍamma on the ḍād; and with fatḥa on the ʿayn, and with ḍamma on it, together with sukūn on the ḍād. The original is the first; the second is a lightening, and in the third there is a transfer [of the vowel]. It was not made plural because the plural here has the status of the singular, since the meaning is that all the misleaders together are not fit to stand, in being relied upon for support, in the place of a single one. It may also be that the singular was made to suffice instead of the plural.

ukberi-tibyan:52-52.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ نَادُوا شُرَكَائِيَ الَّذِينَ زَعَمْتُمْ فَدَعَوْهُمْ فَلَمْ يَسْتَجِيبُوا لَهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُمْ مَوْبِقًا (٥٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ): i.e. "and mention the day He says". It is read with nūn and with yāʾ.
And (بَيْنَهُمْ): an adverb (ẓarf). It is also said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "and We made their connection a destruction for them".
And (الْمَوْبِقُ): a noun of place; or, if you wish, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun). One says «وَبَقَ يَبِقُ وُبُوقًا وَمَوْبِقًا», and «وَبَقَ يَوْبَقُ وَبْقًا».

ukberi-tibyan:53-53.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَأَى الْمُجْرِمُونَ النَّارَ فَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ مُوَاقِعُوهَا وَلَمْ يَجِدُوا عَنْهَا مَصْرِفًا (٥٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَصْرِفًا): i.e. «انْصِرَافًا» (a turning away).
It may also be a noun of place, i.e. they found no place to which one could turn away from it. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:54-54.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَا فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ لِلنَّاسِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ وَكَانَ الْإِنْسَانُ أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا (٥٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ): i.e. "We have struck for them a parable of every kind of parable"; the object is omitted. Or it may be explained according to the view of al-Akhfash, that «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).
(أَكْثَرَ شَيْءٍ جَدَلًا): concerning it there are two views:
The first: «شَيْء» here has the sense of «مُجَادِل» (one who disputes), because «أَفْعَل» [the elative] is annexed to that of which it is a part, and its specification (tamyīz) by «جَدَلًا» requires that the one who is "most" be a disputer; this is a case of putting the general in place of the specific.
The second: there is an omission in the sentence, its implied form being "and the disputing of man is the most of anything", after which He specified it [with the tamyīz].

ukberi-tibyan:55-55.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا مَنَعَ النَّاسَ أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا إِذْ جَاءَهُمُ الْهُدَى وَيَسْتَغْفِرُوا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَّا أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ الْأَوَّلِينَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ قُبُلًا (٥٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يُؤْمِنُوا): the object of «مَنَعَ», and «أَنْ تَأْتِيَهُمْ» is its fāʿil (agent). There is an omitted muḍāf (first term of the construct) in it, i.e. "except the seeking of, or the awaiting of, its coming to them".

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا نُرْسِلُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنْذِرِينَ وَيُجَادِلُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِالْبَاطِلِ لِيُدْحِضُوا بِهِ الْحَقَّ وَاتَّخَذُوا آيَاتِي وَمَا أُنْذِرُوا هُزُوًا (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَمَا أُنْذِرُوا): «مَا» means «الَّذِي» (that which), and the returning pronoun (ʿāʾid) is omitted; «هُزُوًا» is a second object.
«مَا» may also be maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun with what follows).

ukberi-tibyan:57-57.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ ذُكِّرَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِ فَأَعْرَضَ عَنْهَا وَنَسِيَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِي آذَانِهِمْ وَقْرًا وَإِنْ تَدْعُهُمْ إِلَى الْهُدَى فَلَنْ يَهْتَدُوا إِذًا أَبَدًا (٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ يَفْقَهُوهُ): i.e. "out of aversion to their understanding it".

ukberi-tibyan:58-58.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَبُّكَ الْغَفُورُ ذُو الرَّحْمَةِ لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُمْ بِمَا كَسَبُوا لَعَجَّلَ لَهُمُ الْعَذَابَ بَلْ لَهُمْ مَوْعِدٌ لَنْ يَجِدُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ مَوْئِلًا (٥٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَوْ يُؤَاخِذُهُمْ): an imperfect verb narrating a present state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl); it is also said: it has the sense of the past. «الْمَوْعِد» here is suitable [to be taken] as a noun of place and as a maṣdar (verbal noun).
And «الْمَوْئِل» is of the pattern «مَفْعِل», from «وَأَلَ يَئِلُ» when one takes refuge; it too is suitable for both.

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتِلْكَ الْقُرَى أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ لَمَّا ظَلَمُوا وَجَعَلْنَا لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ مَوْعِدًا (٥٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَتِلْكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ» is the khabar (predicate). «تِلْكَ» may also be in the position of the accusative by an implied (muqaddar) verb which the one mentioned explains. And (لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ): of the pattern «مُفْعَل», with ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the lām; concerning it there are two views:
The first: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning «الْإِهْلَاك» (destroying), like «الْمُدْخَل». The second: it is a passive participle (mafʿūl), i.e. "for whoever was destroyed", or "for what was destroyed of them".
It is also read with fatḥa on both [mīm and lām]; it is then the maṣdar of «هَلَكَ يَهْلِكُ».
And it is read with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the lām; this too is a maṣdar. It may also be a noun of time. It is annexed to the agent; it may also be [annexed] to the object, according to the dialect of those who say «هَلَكْتُهُ أُهْلِكُهُ», and «الْمَوْعِد» is a noun of time.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذْ قَالَ مُوسَى لِفَتَاهُ لَا أَبْرَحُ حَتَّى أَبْلُغَ مَجْمَعَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ أَوْ أَمْضِيَ حُقُبًا (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَإِذْ قَالَ): i.e. "and mention". (لَا أَبْرَحُ): concerning it there are two views. The first: it is the defective [verb] (nāqiṣa, of the kāna type), and concerning its noun and its khabar (predicate) there are two views. The first: its khabar is omitted, i.e. "I shall not cease travelling". The second: the khabar is «حَتَّى أَبْلَغَ», and the implied form is "my travelling shall not cease"; then the noun was omitted and the pronoun of the speaker was made a substitute for it, so the verb was ascribed to the speaker.
The other view: it is the complete [verb] (tāmma), and the object is omitted, i.e. "I shall not leave off travelling until I reach", as when you say «لَا أَبْرَحُ الْمَكَانَ», i.e. "I shall not leave it".
(أَوْ أَمْضِيَ): concerning «أَوْ» there are two views:
The first: it is for one of two things, i.e. "I shall travel until one of the two occurs: either reaching the meeting-place or the passing of long ages". The second: it is in the sense of «إِلَّا أَنْ» (unless), i.e. "unless I spend a time in which I become certain that the meeting-place of the two seas has been missed". «الْمَجْمَع» is an adverb (ẓarf). It is also read with kasra on the second mīm, by analogy with «الْمَغْرِب» and «الْمَطْلِع».

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَلَمَّا بَلَغَا مَجْمَعَ بَيْنِهِمَا نَسِيَا حُوتَهُمَا فَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ سَرَبًا (٦١))
His saying, Exalted is He: (سَبِيلَهُ): the hāʾ refers back to the fish.
And (فِي الْبَحْرِ): it may be attached to «اتَّخَذَ», or be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «السَّبِيل», or from «سَرَبًا».

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَا إِلَى الصَّخْرَةِ فَإِنِّي نَسِيتُ الْحُوتَ وَمَا أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلَّا الشَّيْطَانُ أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ وَاتَّخَذَ سَبِيلَهُ فِي الْبَحْرِ عَجَبًا (٦٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ): in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) from the hāʾ in «أَنْسَانِيهِ», i.e. "nothing made me forget to mention it [but Satan]". Kasra and ḍamma on the hāʾ are both permissible, and it has been read with both.
(عَجَبًا): the second object of «اتَّخَذَ». It is also said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. Moses said: "How wondrous!"; on this view the second object of «اتَّخَذَ» is «فِي الْبَحْرِ».

ukberi-tibyan:64-65.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ ذَلِكَ مَا كُنَّا نَبْغِ فَارْتَدَّا عَلَى آثَارِهِمَا قَصَصًا فَوَجَدَا عَبْدًا مِنْ عِبَادِنَا آتَيْنَاهُ رَحْمَةً مِنْ عِنْدِنَا وَعَلَّمْنَاهُ مِنْ لَدُنَّا عِلْمًا (٦).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نَبْغِي): the best is to keep the yāʾ; it has also been read with it dropped, by analogy with the verse-endings (fawāṣil); what made this easy is that the yāʾ does not take a ḍamma here.
(قَصَصًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) of «فَارْتَدَّا» according to the meaning. It is also said: it is the maṣdar of an omitted verb, i.e. "following [their tracks] closely". It is also said: it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. «مُقْتَصِّينَ» (tracing). And «عِلْمًا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); had it been a maṣdar it would have been «تَعْلِيمًا».

ukberi-tibyan:66-66.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لَهُ مُوسَى هَلْ أَتَّبِعُكَ عَلَى أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِي مِمَّا عُلِّمْتَ رُشْدًا (٦٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عَلَى أَنْ تُعَلِّمَنِي): it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "I follow you with my humbling myself", and the kāf is the one the ḥāl describes (ṣāḥib al-ḥāl).
And (رَشَدًا): the object of «تُعَلِّمَنِ».
It cannot be the object of «عُلِّمْتَ», because there would then be no returning pronoun referring to «الَّذِي» [i.e. to «مَا»]; nor is it a ḥāl from the omitted returning pronoun, because the meaning on that view would be far-fetched.
«الرُّشْد» and «الرَّشَد» are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:68-68.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَيْفَ تَصْبِرُ عَلَى مَا لَمْ تُحِطْ بِهِ خُبْرًا (٦٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (خُبْرًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun) [mafʿūl muṭlaq], because «تُحِيطُ» has the sense of «تُخْبِرُ» (have knowledge of).

ukberi-tibyan:70-70.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ فَإِنِ اتَّبَعْتَنِي فَلَا تَسْأَلْنِي عَنْ شَيْءٍ حَتَّى أُحْدِثَ لَكَ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا (٧٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَسْأَلْنِي): it is read with sukūn on the lām, a light nūn, and the yāʾ kept. And with fatḥa on the lām and a doubled nūn, the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) being dropped. It may also be that the light [energetic] nūn has entered upon the nūn of protection. And it is read with fatḥa on the nūn and doubled.

ukberi-tibyan:71-71.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّى إِذَا رَكِبَا فِي السَّفِينَةِ خَرَقَهَا قَالَ أَخَرَقْتَهَا لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا إِمْرًا (٧١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لِتُغْرِقَ أَهْلَهَا): it is read with tāʾ as an address, both doubled and light; and with yāʾ, with the agent named [i.e. «لِيَغْرَقَ أَهْلُهَا», "so that its people drown"].

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ لَا تُؤَاخِذْنِي بِمَا نَسِيتُ وَلَا تُرْهِقْنِي مِنْ أَمْرِي عُسْرًا (٧٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (عُسْرًا): it is the second object of «تُرْهِقْ», because the meaning is "do not make me undergo" or "do not cover me with".

ukberi-tibyan:74-74.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّى إِذَا لَقِيَا غُلَامًا فَقَتَلَهُ قَالَ أَقَتَلْتَ نَفْسًا زَكِيَّةً بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ لَقَدْ جِئْتَ شَيْئًا نُكْرًا (٧٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ): the bāʾ is attached to «قَتَلْتَ», i.e. "you killed him without cause".
It may also be attached to an omitted [word], i.e. "a killing without [the taking of] a soul"; or it may be in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "you killed him wrongfully" or "him being wronged".
«النُّكْر» and «النُّكُر» are two dialectal forms, and it has been read with both. And (شَيْئًا): an object, i.e. "you have brought about a reprehensible thing".
It may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a reprehensible coming".

ukberi-tibyan:76-76.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ إِنْ سَأَلْتُكَ عَنْ شَيْءٍ بَعْدَهَا فَلَا تُصَاحِبْنِي قَدْ بَلَغْتَ مِنْ لَدُنِّي عُذْرًا (٧٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْ لَدُنِّي): it is read with a doubled nūn, the noun being «لَدُنْ» and the second nūn being [the nūn] of protection (wiqāya). And with it light, concerning which there are two views:
The first: it is the same, except that the nūn of protection was dropped, just as they said «قَدْنِي» and «قَدِي». The second: its origin is «لَدُ», which is a dialectal form of it, and the nūn is for protection.
And (عُذْرًا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as when you say "you have reached the goal".

ukberi-tibyan:77-77.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَانْطَلَقَا حَتَّى إِذَا أَتَيَا أَهْلَ قَرْيَةٍ اسْتَطْعَمَا أَهْلَهَا فَأَبَوْا أَنْ يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًا يُرِيدُ أَنْ يَنْقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُ قَالَ لَوْ شِئْتَ لَاتَّخَذْتَ عَلَيْهِ أَجْرًا (٧٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (اسْتَطْعَمَا أَهْلَهَا): it is the apodosis (jawāb) of «إِذَا»; the mention of «الْأَهْل» was repeated for emphasis.
(أَنْ يَنْقَضَّ): with the dotted ḍād, doubled, without an alif; it is from falling, likened to the swooping (inqiḍāḍ) of a bird.
It is also read with the light form, as a passive (mā lam yusamma fāʿiluhu), from «النَّقْض» (demolishing).
And it is read with an alif and doubling, like «يَحْمَارُّ».
And it is read likewise without doubling; this is from your saying «انْقَاضَ الْبِنَاءُ» when the building collapsed, and it is [of the pattern] «يَنْفَعِلُ».
And it is read with the ḍād doubled, from your saying «انْقَاضَّتِ السِّنُّ» when the tooth broke. [Translator's note: this repeats the reading with alif and doubling given above; the source may have intended the undotted ṣād here («يَنْقَاصَّ»), but it is translated as written.]
(لَاتَّخَذْتَ): it is read with kasra on the khāʾ, light [«لَتَخِذْتَ»]; it is from «تَخِذَ يَتَّخِذُ», when one does something.
And it is read with doubling and fatḥa on the khāʾ; concerning this there are two views. The first: it is «افْتَعَلَ» from «تَخِذَهُ».
The second: it is from «الْأَخْذ», its original form being «ايْتَخَذَ»; the yāʾ was replaced by a tāʾ and assimilated, and the original of the yāʾ is the hamza.

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هَذَا فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنِكَ سَأُنَبِّئُكَ بِتَأْوِيلِ مَا لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ عَلَيْهِ صَبْرًا (٧٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي): the majority [read it] with annexation (iḍāfa), i.e. "the severing of our bond".
It is also read with tanwīn [«فِرَاقٌ بَيْنِي»], «بَيْنَ» being accusative as an adverb (ẓarf).

ukberi-tibyan:79-79.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمَّا السَّفِينَةُ فَكَانَتْ لِمَسَاكِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ فِي الْبَحْرِ فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أَعِيبَهَا وَكَانَ وَرَاءَهُمْ مَلِكٌ يَأْخُذُ كُلَّ سَفِينَةٍ غَصْبًا (٧٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (غَصْبًا): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a maṣdar taken from the meaning of it [i.e. of «يَأْخُذُ», as an absolute object].

ukberi-tibyan:80-80.t:
Allah the Exalted says: {وَأما الْغُلَام فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤمنين فَخَشِينَا أَن يرهقهما طغيانا وَكفرا}
His saying, Exalted is He: (مُؤْمِنَيْنِ): the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ». It is read irregularly (shādhdh) with the alif [«مُؤْمِنَانِ»], on the basis that in «كَانَ» there is a pronoun referring to the boy, or the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and the clause after it is its khabar.

ukberi-tibyan:81-81.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَرَدْنَا أَنْ يُبْدِلَهُمَا رَبُّهُمَا خَيْرًا مِنْهُ زَكَاةً وَأَقْرَبَ رُحْمًا (٨١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (زَكَاةً): a tamyīz (specification), governed by «خَيْرًا مِنْهُ».
And (رُحْمًا): likewise. Sukūn and ḍamma [on the ḥāʾ] are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:82-82.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَمَّا الْجِدَارُ فَكَانَ لِغُلَامَيْنِ يَتِيمَيْنِ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ وَكَانَ تَحْتَهُ كَنْزٌ لَهُمَا وَكَانَ أَبُوهُمَا صَالِحًا فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَنْ يَبْلُغَا أَشُدَّهُمَا وَيَسْتَخْرِجَا كَنْزَهُمَا رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ وَمَا فَعَلْتُهُ عَنْ أَمْرِي ذَلِكَ تَأْوِيلُ مَا لَمْ تَسْطِعْ عَلَيْهِ صَبْرًا (٨٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (رَحْمَةً مِنْ رَبِّكَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), or [in the] position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:83-83.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنْ ذِي الْقَرْنَيْنِ قُلْ سَأَتْلُو عَلَيْكُمْ مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا (٨٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مِنْهُ ذِكْرًا): i.e. "of his reports"; the muḍāf (first term of the construct) was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:84-84.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَآتَيْنَاهُ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ سَبَبًا (٨٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَكَّنَّا لَهُ): the object is omitted, i.e. "his affair".

ukberi-tibyan:85-85.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَأَتْبَعَ سَبَبًا (٨٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَأَتْبَعَ): it is transmitted with a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) and doubling [«فَاتَّبَعَ»], with «سَبَبًا» as its object. And it is read with a disjunctive hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and the light form, in which case it takes two objects, i.e. "he made one means follow another means".

ukberi-tibyan:86-86.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ الشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِي عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍ وَوَجَدَ عِنْدَهَا قَوْمًا قُلْنَا يَا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ وَإِمَّا أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ فِيهِمْ حُسْنًا (٧٨٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَمِئَةٍ): it is read with hamza and without alif; it is from «حَمِئَتِ الْبِئْرُ تَحْمَأُ», when the well came to contain «حَمْأَة», which is black mud. The hamza may also be lightened.
And it is read with alif and without hamza [«حَامِيَةٍ»]; this too is a lightened form of the hamzated word. It may also be from «حَمِيَ الْمَاءُ», when the water's heat became intense, as in His saying, Exalted is He: (نَارًا حَامِيَةً).
(إِمَّا أَنْ تُعَذِّبَ): «أَنْ» [with its verb] is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "either punishment is to befall them from you". It is also said: it is a khabar, i.e. "either it is that you punish", or "either the matter is that you punish". It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative, i.e. "either you bring about that you punish, or you do [good]".
(حَسَنًا): i.e. "a matter possessing goodness".

ukberi-tibyan:88-88.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَأَمَّا مَنْ آمَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَلَهُ جَزَاءً الْحُسْنَى وَسَنَقُولُ لَهُ مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا (٨٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (جَزَاءً الْحُسْنَى): it is read with the nominative and annexation (iḍāfa) [«جَزَاءُ الْحُسْنَى»]; it is then a mubtadaʾ (subject), or made nominative by the adverbial phrase (ẓarf), and the implied form is "he shall have the reward of the best trait".
And it is read with the nominative and tanwīn [«جَزَاءٌ الْحُسْنَى»], «الْحُسْنَى» being a badal (substitute) or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ.
And it is read with the accusative and tanwīn, i.e. "he shall have the best as a reward"; it is then a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "being rewarded with it". It is also said: it is a maṣdar according to the meaning, i.e. "he is rewarded with it with a reward". It is also said: a tamyīz (specification).
And it is read with the accusative without tanwīn; this is like the tanwīn form, except that the tanwīn was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(مِنْ أَمْرِنَا يُسْرًا): i.e. "something possessing ease".

ukberi-tibyan:90-90.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ الشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَى قَوْمٍ لَمْ نَجْعَلْ لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهَا سِتْرًا (٩٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَطْلِعَ الشَّمْسِ): it may be a noun of place, or it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the muḍāf (first term of the construct) omitted, i.e. "the place of the sun's rising".

ukberi-tibyan:91-91.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (كَذَلِكَ وَقَدْ أَحَطْنَا بِمَا لَدَيْهِ خُبْرًا (٩١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is thus".
It may also be an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:93-93.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (حَتَّى إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِنْ دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًا لَا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًا (٩٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ): «بَيْنَ» here is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
«السَّدّ» with fatḥa is the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «سَدَّ», and it has the sense of the thing blocked [i.e. the barrier]; with ḍamma it is a noun for the thing blocked. It is also said: the form with ḍamma is what is of Allah's creation, and the form with fatḥa is what is of human making. It is also said: they are two dialectal forms with one meaning; and it has been read with both.

ukberi-tibyan:94-94.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالُوا يَا ذَا الْقَرْنَيْنِ إِنَّ يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ مُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَهَلْ نَجْعَلُ لَكَ خَرْجًا عَلَى أَنْ تَجْعَلَ بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَهُمْ سَدًّا (٩٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ): they are two foreign names, diptotes because of foreignness and definiteness; they may be pronounced with or without the hamza. It is also said: they are Arabic, «يَأْجُوج» being of the pattern «يَفْعُول», like «يَرْبُوع», and «مَأْجُوج» of the pattern «مَفْعُول», like «مَعْقُول»; both are from «أَجَّ الظَّلِيمُ» (the male ostrich ran fast), or from «أَجَّتِ النَّارُ» when the fire blazed; [on this view] they are diptotes because of definiteness and femininity. And «الْخَرْج» is read without alif, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of «خَرَجَ», and what is meant by it is payment.
It is also said: it has the sense of «مُخْرَج» (what is paid out). And «الْخَرَاج», with alif, also has the sense of payment.
It is also said: it is the money levied on land or on persons.

ukberi-tibyan:95-96.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ مَا مَكَّنِّي فِيهِ رَبِّي خَيْرٌ فَأَعِينُونِي بِقُوَّةٍ أَجْعَلْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُمْ رَدْمًا (٩٥) آتُونِي زُبَرَ الْحَدِيدِ حَتَّى إِذَا سَاوَى بَيْنَ الصَّدَفَيْنِ قَالَ انْفُخُوا حَتَّى إِذَا جَعَلَهُ نَارًا قَالَ آتُونِي أُفْرِغْ عَلَيْهِ قِطْرًا (٩٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَا مَكَّنِّي فِيهِ): it is read with doubling by assimilation (idghām), and with the letters pronounced separately (iẓhār) according to the original. «مَا» means «الَّذِي» (that which); it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «خَيْرٌ» is its khabar (predicate).
(بِقُوَّةٍ): i.e. "with men possessing — or [men] possessing (dhawī) — strength", or "with something by which strength is gained". «الرَّدْم» has the sense of what is used for filling up, or of the one who fills up. (آتُونِي): it is read with a disjunctive hamza and lengthening, i.e. "give me"; and with a connecting hamza [«ائْتُونِي»], i.e. "come to me", the implied form being "with pieces of iron"; or it is in the sense of «أَحْضِرُوا» (bring), because «جَاءَ» and «حَضَرَ» are close in meaning. And (الصَّدَفَيْنِ): it is read with two ḍammas; with ḍamma on the first and sukūn on the second; with two fatḥas; with fatḥa on the first and sukūn on the second; and with fatḥa on the first and ḍamma on the second. All of them are dialectal forms, and «الصَّدَف» is the side of a mountain. (قِطْرًا): the object of «آتُونِي», and the object of «أُفْرِغْ» is omitted, i.e. "that I may pour it". The Kufans said: it is the object of «أُفْرِغْ», and the object of the first [verb] is omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:97-97.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَمَا اسْطَاعُوا أَنْ يَظْهَرُوهُ وَمَا اسْتَطَاعُوا لَهُ نَقْبًا (٩٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَمَا اسْطَاعُوا): it is read with a light ṭāʾ, i.e. «اسْتَطَاعُوا», the tāʾ having been dropped for lightness.
And it is read with the ṭāʾ doubled, which is far-fetched because it involves the meeting of two quiescent letters.

ukberi-tibyan:98-98.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قَالَ هَذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّي فَإِذَا جَاءَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي جَعَلَهُ دَكَّاءَ وَكَانَ وَعْدُ رَبِّي حَقًّا (٩٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (دَكَّاءَ), and «دَكًّا»: this has been mentioned in [Sūrat] al-Aʿrāf.

ukberi-tibyan:101-101.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الَّذِينَ كَانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ فِي غِطَاءٍ عَنْ ذِكْرِي وَكَانُوا لَا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَمْعًا (١٠١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (الَّذِينَ كَانَتْ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective of «الْكَافِرِينَ», or of the accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean), or of the nominative by an implied «هُمْ» (they are).

ukberi-tibyan:102-102.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا عِبَادِي مِنْ دُونِي أَوْلِيَاءَ إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلْكَافِرِينَ نُزُلًا (١٠٢))
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَحَسِبَ): it is read with kasra on the sīn, on the basis that it is a verb.
(أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا): it stands in place of the two objects.
And it is read with sukūn on the sīn and the bāʾ in the nominative [«أَفَحَسْبُ»], as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being «أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا».

ukberi-tibyan:103-103.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ أَعْمَالًا (١٠٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (هَلْ نُنَبِّئُكُمْ): it is read with the letters pronounced separately (iẓhār) according to the original, and with assimilation (idghām) because the points of articulation of the two letters are close.
(أَعْمَالًا): a tamyīz (specification); its being plural is permissible because it is accusative after nouns of agents [i.e. the plural «الْأَخْسَرِينَ»].

ukberi-tibyan:105-105.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ وَلِقَائِهِ فَحَبِطَتْ أَعْمَالُهُمْ فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَزْنًا (١٠٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (فَلَا نُقِيمُ لَهُمْ): it is read with nūn and with yāʾ, and that is clear.
And it is read «يُقَوِّمُ», with a latent agent, i.e. "it does not set a value on their deeds", or "their striving", or "their handiwork".
And (وَزْنًا): a tamyīz (specification) or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:106-106.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ذَلِكَ جَزَاؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ بِمَا كَفَرُوا وَاتَّخَذُوا آيَاتِي وَرُسُلِي هُزُوًا (١٠٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is that", and what follows it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).
«ذَلِكَ» may also be a mubtadaʾ, «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «جَهَنَّمُ» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the first, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "their reward for it".
«ذَلِكَ» may also be a mubtadaʾ, with «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and «جَهَنَّمُ» the khabar.
«جَهَنَّمُ» may also be a badal from «جَزَاء», or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is Hell".
And (بِمَا كَفَرُوا): the khabar of «ذَلِكَ». The bāʾ cannot be attached to «جَزَاؤُهُمْ» because of the separation between them by «جَهَنَّمُ».
And (اتَّخَذُوا): it may be conjoined to «كَفَرُوا», or be resumptive (mustaʾnaf).

ukberi-tibyan:107-107.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ كَانَتْ لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ الْفِرْدَوْسِ نُزُلًا (١٠٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (نُزُلًا): it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «جَنَّاتٍ», with «لَهُمْ» as the khabar (predicate). Or «نُزُلًا» may be the khabar of «كَانَ», and «لَهُمْ» is attached to «كَانَ», or to the khabar, or is for clarification (tabyīn).

ukberi-tibyan:108-108.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا لَا يَبْغُونَ عَنْهَا حِوَلًا (١٠٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (لَا يَبْغُونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «خَالِدِينَ». «الْحِوَل» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning «التَّحَوُّل» (moving away).

ukberi-tibyan:109-109.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ لَوْ كَانَ الْبَحْرُ مِدَادًا لِكَلِمَاتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ الْبَحْرُ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَنْفَدَ كَلِمَاتُ رَبِّي وَلَوْ جِئْنَا بِمِثْلِهِ مَدَدًا (١٠٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَدَدًا): it is a tamyīz (specification); and «مِدَادًا», with alif, is like it in meaning.

ukberi-tibyan:110-110.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَنَا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُكُمْ يُوحَى إِلَيَّ أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ فَمَنْ كَانَ يَرْجُو لِقَاءَ رَبِّهِ فَلْيَعْمَلْ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا وَلَا يُشْرِكْ بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ أَحَدًا (١١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنَّمَا إِلَهُكُمْ): «أَنَّ» here is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), and the entry of the restraining «مَا» (mā al-kāffa) upon it does not prevent that. And (بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ): i.e. "in the worship of his Lord".
It [the bāʾ] may also have its usual sense, i.e. "because of the worship of his Lord". And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:1-2.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَنْزَلَ عَلَى عَبْدِهِ الْكِتَابَ وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ عِوَجًا (١) قَيِّمًا لِيُنْذِرَ بَأْسًا شَدِيدًا مِنْ لَدُنْهُ وَيُبَشِّرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ الَّذِينَ يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحَاتِ أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْرًا حَسَنًا (٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (قَيِّمًا): there are two views on it. The first: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْكِتَاب», placed after its proper position, i.e. "He sent down the Book upright". They said: there is weakness in this, because it entails separating part of the ṣila (relative clause) from another part, since His saying, exalted is He, (وَلَمْ) is conjoined to «أَنْزَلَ». It has also been said: «قَيِّمًا» is a ḥāl, and «وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ» is another ḥāl. The second view: «قَيِّمًا» is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "He made it upright"; so it is also a ḥāl. It has also been said: it is likewise a ḥāl, from the hāʾ in «وَلَمْ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ»; and the ḥāl is corroborative (muʾakkida); it has also been said: transitory (muntaqila).
His saying, exalted is He: (لِيُنْذِرَ): i.e. "that He may warn the servants", or "that He may warn you". (مِنْ لَدُنْهُ): it is read with fatḥa on the lām, ḍamma on the dāl and sukūn on the nūn, which is a dialectal form. And it is read with fatḥa on the lām, ḍamma on the dāl and kasra on the nūn. Some of them slur (ikhtilās) the ḍamma of the dāl, and some of them slur the kasra of the nūn.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَاكِثِينَ فِيهِ أَبَدًا (٣)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مَاكِثِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun in «لَهُمْ», what governs it being the [implied] notion of settledness (al-istiqrār). It has also been said: it is an adjective (ṣifa) of «أَجْر», the returning pronoun being the hāʾ in «فِيهِ».

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (مَا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلَا لِآبَائِهِمْ كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ إِنْ يَقُولُونَ إِلَّا كَذِبًا (٥) فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ عَلَى آثَارِهِمْ إِنْ لَمْ يُؤْمِنُوا بِهَذَا الْحَدِيثِ أَسَفًا (٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (كَبُرَتْ): the majority read with ḍamma on the bāʾ; it has also been given sukūn for lightness.
And (كَلِمَةً): a tamyīz (specification), the fāʿil (agent) being latent (muḍmar), i.e. "their statement is grievous".
And regarding (تَخْرُجُ) there are two views. The first: it is in the position of the accusative as an adjective (ṣifa) of «كَلِمَة». The second: it is in the position of the nominative, its implied form being "a word that comes out (كَلِمَةٌ تَخْرُجُ)", because «كَبُرَ» is in the sense of «بِئْسَ», so what is omitted is the one specified for blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm). And (كَذِبًا): the object of «يَقُولُونَ», or an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a lying statement".
And (أَسَفًا): a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «بَاخِعٌ». It has also been said: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The majority read «إِنْ لَمْ» with kasra, as a condition; and it is read with fatḥa [«أَنْ لَمْ»], i.e. "because they do not believe".

ukberi-tibyan:7-7.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا مَا عَلَى الْأَرْضِ زِينَةً لَهَا لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ أَيُّهُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا (٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (زِينَةً): a second object, on the view that «جَعَلَ» means «صَيَّرَ» (made into); or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose); or a ḥāl (circumstantial), on the view that «جَعَلَ» means «خَلَقَ» (created).

ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمْ حَسِبْتَ أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ الْكَهْفِ وَالرَّقِيمِ كَانُوا مِنْ آيَاتِنَا عَجَبًا (٩) إِذْ أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِنْ لَدُنْكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا (١٠)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَمْ حَسِبْتَ): its implied form is "rather, did you think? (بَلْ أَحَسِبْتَ)". (وَالرَّقِيمِ): in the sense of «الْمَرْقُوم» (the inscribed), according to those who take it to be a writing.
And «عَجَبًا» is the khabar (predicate) of «كَانَ», and (مِنْ آيَاتِنَا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from it. It is also possible that both are predicates. It is also possible that «عَجَبًا» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in the preposition phrase.
His saying, exalted is He: (إِذْ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «عَجَبًا». It is also possible that the implied form is "remember when".

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَى آذَانِهِمْ فِي الْكَهْفِ سِنِينَ عَدَدًا (١١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (سِنِينَ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «ضَرَبْنَا», which is in the sense of "We put them to sleep".
And (عَدَدًا): an adjective (ṣifa) of «سِنِين», i.e. "counted", or "possessing a number". It has also been said: a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they are counted a counting".

ukberi-tibyan:12-12.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ثُمَّ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَى لِمَا لَبِثُوا أَمَدًا (١٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (أَيُّ الْحِزْبَيْنِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «أَحْصَى» is the khabar (predicate); the position of the clause is accusative by «نَعْلَمَ». Regarding «أَحْصَى» there are two views. The first: it is a past verb, and «أَمَدًا» is its object; «لِمَا لَبِثُوا» is a naʿt (adjective) of it placed before it, so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "on account of their staying". It has also been said: the lām is redundant (zāʾida), «مَا» means «الَّذِي», and «أَمَدًا» is the object of «لَبِثُوا»; this is a mistake. Rather, the proper way is for it to be a tamyīz (specification), the implied form being "of what they stayed (لِمَا لَبِثُوهُ)". The second view: it is a noun [an elative], and «أَمَدًا» is accusative by a verb indicated by the noun; «أَحْصَى» came with the augment dropped, just as there came "he is most giving of wealth (أَعْطَى لِلْمَالِ)" and "most deserving of good (أَوْلَى بِالْخَيْرِ)".

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَرَبَطْنَا عَلَى قُلُوبِهِمْ إِذْ قَامُوا فَقَالُوا رَبُّنَا رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ لَنْ نَدْعُوَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَهًا لَقَدْ قُلْنَا إِذًا شَطَطًا (١٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (شَطَطًا): a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); or the implied form is "an outrageous statement (قَوْلًا شَطَطًا)".

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (هَؤُلَاءِ قَوْمُنَا اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ آلِهَةً لَوْلَا يَأْتُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِسُلْطَانٍ بَيِّنٍ فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ افْتَرَى عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا (١٥)).
His saying, exalted is He: (هَؤُلَاءِ): a mubtadaʾ (subject); (قَوْمُنَا) is an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); and «اتَّخَذُوا» is the khabar (predicate).

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا اللَّهَ فَأْوُوا إِلَى الْكَهْفِ يَنْشُرْ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ وَيُهَيِّئْ لَكُمْ مِنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِرْفَقًا (١٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَإِذِ اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for an omitted verb, i.e. "and some of them said to others …". (وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ): regarding «مَا» there are three views. The first: it is a noun meaning «الَّذِي», and «إِلَّا اللَّهَ» is excepted from «مَا» or from the omitted returning pronoun. The second: it is maṣdariyya (verbal-noun forming), the implied form being: "you have withdrawn from them and from their worship, except the worship of Allah". The third: it is a negative particle; then two views arise regarding the exception. The first: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ). The second: it is connected (muttaṣil), the implied form being: "and when you have withdrawn from them, except the worship of Allah", or "and they do not worship except Allah", for they used to worship Allah along with the idols, or among them were some who worshipped Allah.
(مِرفَقًا): it is read with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the fāʾ, because it is something by which one is helped; so it is like a transferred noun used [for an instrument], like «الْمِبْرَد» (the file) and «الْمُنْخُل» (the sieve).
And it is read the other way round [«مَرْفِقًا»], and it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a benefit (ارْتِفَاقًا)".
There is a third dialectal form, with fatḥa on both [«مَرْفَقًا»], and it is also a maṣdar, like «الْمَضْرَب» and «الْمَنْزَع».

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَتْ تَزَاوَرُ عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَتْ تَقْرِضُهُمْ ذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ وَهُمْ فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِنْهُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آيَاتِ اللَّهِ مَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِي وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ وَلِيًّا مُرْشِدًا (١٧)).
His saying, exalted is He: (تَزَاوَرُ): it is read with doubling of the zāy [«تَزَّاوَرُ»], its origin being «تَتَزَاوَرُ»; the second [tāʾ] was changed into a zāy and assimilated.
And it is read without doubling [«تَزَاوَرُ»], with the second [tāʾ] dropped. And it is read with doubling of the rāʾ [«تَزْوَرُّ»], like «تَحْمَرُّ»; and it is read with an alif after the wāw [«تَزْوَارُّ»], like «تَحْمَارُّ». And it is read with a hamza with kasra between the wāw and the rāʾ [«تَزْوَئِرُّ»], like «تَطْمَئِنُّ».
And (ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ): an adverb (ẓarf) for «تَزَاوَرُ».

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ أَيْقَاظًا وَهُمْ رُقُودٌ وَنُقَلِّبُهُمْ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ وَكَلْبُهُمْ بَاسِطٌ ذِرَاعَيْهِ بِالْوَصِيدِ لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ لَوَلَّيْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِرَارًا وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ رُعْبًا (١٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَنُقَلِّبُهُمْ): the well-known reading is that it is a verb attributed to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
And it is read with a tāʾ, ḍamma on the lām and fatḥa on the bāʾ [«وَتَقَلُّبَهُمْ»], and it is accusative by a verb indicated by the speech, i.e. "and We see their turning about".
And (بَاسِطٌ): the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject), and «ذِرَاعَيْهِ» is accusative by it. The active participle governs here even though it refers to the past only because it is a narrated ḥāl (ḥāl maḥkiyya).
(لَوِ اطَّلَعْتَ): with kasra on the wāw, according to the base; and with ḍamma [«لَوُ اطَّلَعْتَ»], so that it is of the same kind as the wāw.
(فِرَارًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), because «وَلَّيْتَ» means «فَرَرْتَ» (you fled).
It may also be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), or a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose).
(لَمُلِئْتَ): without doubling; and it is read with doubling [«لَمُلِّئْتَ»], for intensiveness.
And (رُعْبًا): a second object. It has also been said: a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:19-19.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ بَعَثْنَاهُمْ لِيَتَسَاءَلُوا بَيْنَهُمْ قَالَ قَائِلٌ مِنْهُمْ كَمْ لَبِثْتُمْ قَالُوا لَبِثْنَا يَوْمًا أَوْ بَعْضَ يَوْمٍ قَالُوا رَبُّكُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثْتُمْ فَابْعَثُوا أَحَدَكُمْ بِوَرِقِكُمْ هَذِهِ إِلَى الْمَدِينَةِ فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّهَا أَزْكَى طَعَامًا فَلْيَأْتِكُمْ بِرِزْقٍ مِنْهُ وَلْيَتَلَطَّفْ وَلَا يُشْعِرَنَّ بِكُمْ أَحَدًا (١٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَكَذَلِكَ): in the position of the accusative, i.e. "and We raised them just as We have narrated to you".
And (كَمْ): an adverb (ẓarf); and «بِوَرِقِكُمْ» is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). The base form has fatḥa on the wāw and kasra on the rāʾ, and it has been read so, with the qāf pronounced distinctly according to the base, and with it assimilated because its point of articulation is close to that of the kāf; assimilation was preferred because of the many vowels and the kasra.
And it is read with sukūn on the rāʾ [«بِوَرْقِكُمْ»] for lightness; and with sukūn on it and kasra on the wāw [«بِوِرْقِكُمْ»], by transferring the kasra to it, as one says «فَخْذ» and «فَخِذ».
(أَيُّهَا أَزْكَى): the clause is in the position of the accusative, the verb being suspended (muʿallaq) from governing in the wording.
And (طَعَامًا): a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ لِيَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ وَأَنَّ السَّاعَةَ لَا رَيْبَ فِيهَا إِذْ يَتَنَازَعُونَ بَيْنَهُمْ أَمْرَهُمْ فَقَالُوا ابْنُوا عَلَيْهِمْ بُنْيَانًا رَبُّهُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ قَالَ الَّذِينَ غَلَبُوا عَلَى أَمْرِهِمْ لَنَتَّخِذَنَّ عَلَيْهِمْ مَسْجِدًا (٢١)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِذْ يَتَنَازَعُونَ): «إِذْ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «لِيَعْلَمُوا», or for «أَعْثَرْنَا». It is weak for «الْوَعْد» to govern it, because something has already been predicated of it.
It is possible that the meaning of «حَقٌّ» governs it.
(بُنْيَانًا): an object; it is the plural of «بُنْيَانَة». It has also been said: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (سَيَقُولُونَ ثَلَاثَةٌ رَابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ وَيَقُولُونَ خَمْسَةٌ سَادِسُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ رَجْمًا بِالْغَيْبِ وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ قُلْ رَبِّي أَعْلَمُ بِعِدَّتِهِمْ مَا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِمْ إِلَّا مِرَاءً ظَاهِرًا وَلَا تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ مِنْهُمْ أَحَدًا (٢٢)).
His saying, exalted is He: (ثَلَاثَةٌ): it is read irregularly (shādhdh) with a doubled tāʾ, on the basis that the reader gave the thāʾ sukūn, changed it into a tāʾ and assimilated it into the feminine tāʾ, as you say «ابْعَتْ تِلْكَ».
(وَرَابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ): «رَابِعُهُمْ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «كَلْبُهُمْ» its khabar (predicate). The active participle does not govern here, because it refers to the past. The clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of «ثَلَاثَة», not a ḥāl (circumstantial), since there is nothing to govern it; for the implied form is "they are three (هُمْ ثَلَاثَةٌ)", and «هُمْ» does not govern; nor is it valid to supply «هَؤُلَاءِ», because that points to something present, and they were not pointing to something present. Had the wāw been here and in the clause after it, it would have been permissible, just as it was permissible in the last clause, because when a clause occurs as an adjective of an indefinite noun the wāw may enter it. This is the correct view regarding the insertion of the wāw in «وَثَامِنُهُمْ».
It has also been said: it entered to indicate that what follows it is a resumptive (mustaʾnaf) truth, and not of the kind of what is said by guesswork.
Other things have been said about it, and they are of no account.
And (رَجْمًا): a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "they guess a guessing".
[Translator's note: the source quotes the phrase as (وَرَابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ) with a wāw, while the verse as quoted above reads «رَابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ»; the discussion itself treats it as being without the wāw.]

ukberi-tibyan:23-24.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَا تَقُولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذَلِكَ غَدًا (٢٣) إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ وَاذْكُرْ رَبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ وَقُلْ عَسَى أَنْ يَهْدِيَنِي رَبِّي لِأَقْرَبَ مِنْ هَذَا رَشَدًا (٢٤)).
His saying, exalted is He: (إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ): regarding what it is excepted from there are three views. The first: it is from the prohibition, the meaning being: do not say "I will do it tomorrow" unless you are given leave to say it. The second: it is from «فَاعِلٌ», i.e. do not say "I am doing it tomorrow" until you join to it the saying "if Allah wills". The third: it is disconnected (munqaṭiʿ).
The position of «أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ» is accusative, on two views. The first: as an exception, the implied form being: "do not say that at any time except at the time that Allah wills", i.e. gives leave; so "time" was omitted though it is intended.
The second: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being: "do not say 'I will do it tomorrow' except saying 'if Allah wills'"; so the saying was omitted, and that is frequent.
And He made His saying «أَنْ يَشَاءَ» in the sense of «إِنْ شَاءَ»; this is among the things construed according to the meaning.
It has also been said: the implied form is "except with Allah's willing (إِلَّا بِأَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ)", i.e. accompanied by the saying "if Allah wills".

ukberi-tibyan:25-26.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَبِثُوا فِي كَهْفِهِمْ ثَلَاثَمِائَةٍ سِنِينَ وَازْدَادُوا تِسْعًا (٢٥) قُلِ اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا لَبِثُوا لَهُ غَيْبُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ مَا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ مِنْ وَلِيٍّ وَلَا يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَدًا (٢٦)).
His saying, exalted is He: (مِائَةٍ سِنِينَ): it is read with nunation on «مِائَةٍ», and on this reading «سِنِينَ» is a badal (substitute) from «ثَلَاث».
Some permitted it to be a badal from «مِائَة», because «مِائَة» is in the sense of «مِئَات» (hundreds).
And it is read with the genitive construct [«ثَلَاثَمِائَةِ سِنِينَ»]; this is weak in usage, because «مِائَة» is put in construct with a singular; but the reader construed it according to the base, since the base is to put a number in construct with a plural. What strengthens this is that the plural marker here is a compensation for the omission that befell «السَّنَة», so it is as though it were the completion of the singular.
(تِسْعًا): the object of «ازْدَادُوا». «زَادَ» takes two objects, and when it is built on the pattern iftaʿala it takes one.
(أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ): the hāʾ refers back to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and its position is nominative, because the implied form is "Allah saw (أَبْصَرَ اللَّهُ)", the bāʾ being redundant (zāʾida); so it is with the verb of wonder (fiʿl al-taʿajjub) that has the form of the imperative.
Some said: the fāʿil (agent) is latent (muḍmar), the implied form being: "O you who are addressed, bring about seeing regarding the matter of the Cave"; so it is a real imperative.
(وَلَا يُشْرِكُ): it is read with the yāʾ and ḍamma on the kāf, as a statement about Allah; and with the tāʾ [«وَلَا تُشْرِكْ»], as a prohibition, i.e. "O you who are addressed".

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَاصْبِرْ نَفْسَكَ مَعَ الَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ تُرِيدُ زِينَةَ الْحَيَاةِ الدُّنْيَا وَلَا تُطِعْ مَنْ أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِنَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطًا (٢٨)).
His saying, exalted is He: (وَاصْبِرْ): it is transitive, because its meaning is "restrain (احْبِسْ)"; and «بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ» has been mentioned in al-Anʿām.
(وَلَا تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ): the majority attribute the verb to the eyes. Al-Ḥasan read «تُعَدِّ عَيْنَيْكَ», with doubling and without doubling, i.e. do not turn them away.
(أَغْفَلْنَا): the majority read with sukūn on the lām and «قَلْبَهُ» in the accusative, i.e. "We made him heedless as a punishment for him", or "We found him heedless".
And it is read with fatḥa on the lām and «قَلْبُهُ» in the nominative [«أَغْفَلَنَا قَلْبُهُ»], and there are two views on it. The first: "his heart found us turned away from it". The second: "[his heart] neglected our command, [turning away] from remembering us".

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقُلِ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِنْ وَمَنْ شَاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ نَارًا أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا وَإِنْ يَسْتَغِيثُوا يُغَاثُوا بِمَاءٍ كَالْمُهْلِ يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ بِئْسَ الشَّرَابُ وَسَاءَتْ مُرْتَفَقًا (٢٩)).
His saying, exalted is He: (يَشْوِي الْوُجُوهَ): it may be a naʿt (adjective) of «مَاء», or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الْمُهْل», or a ḥāl from the pronoun in the kāf or in the preposition phrase.
And (سَاءَتْ): i.e. the Fire is evil.
(مُرْتَفَقًا): i.e. a place of reclining; or its meaning is: the abode.
